memory_candidates.content: literature-build-index.sh's FTS content_preview field is built from only the first ~500 words of a chunk's source_path file (literature-build-index.sh lines ~228-237). A document's tail content past that word-500 cutoff is invisible to literature-search.sh even though the bytes exist on disk and the chunk's title/section_path may look correct. Before concluding a topic is 'missing' from a document and planning a reconversion, check whether the content already exists past this preview window (grep the source file directly) -- splitting it into its own chunk/file is often sufficient and far lower-risk than a fresh conversion pass.

To splice a missing section span into an existing per-section-chunked literature document (one chunk per paper-section convention, not literature-chunk.sh's token budget): (1) check first whether the text already exists elsewhere in the corpus past the FTS preview window before planning a reconversion; (2) free the needed filename slots by git mv-ing existing sec0N files in STRICTLY DESCENDING numeric order to avoid overwrite collisions; (3) compute new chunk_ids with literature-chunk.sh's own formula sha256(f'{doc_id}\x00{section_path}\x00{content[:64]}').hexdigest()[:16] via a script, never by hand; (4) re-link prev_chunk_id/next_chunk_id only on the two bracketing entries plus the new internal chain; (5) rebuild only the --global index when the repo's specs/literature/ is deprecated/local-db-less.
